candidate.title: Primary FSGS with APOL1 branch
candidate.diseaseDescription: Bounded circulating-factor/immune primary FSGS and separate APOL1-associated kidney injury branch; excludes other genetic, adaptive, viral and drug-associated FSGS. APOL1-associated disease is not classified as idiopathic primary FSGS. Selected mechanistic and intervention reports; not comprehensive literature or treatment coverage.
candidate.releaseNote: Separate study-context views for primary FSGS serum activity, human anti-nephrin findings, experimental immune injury, APOL1 ion transport, transgenic injury, inaxaplin trial and DUPLEX. No universal causal circuit or comprehensive therapy catalogue. Source checks are agent abstract inspections; independent scientific review pending. Selected inaxaplin and sparsentan records added; US sparsentan indication explicitly excludes nephrotic syndrome. Steroids, calcineurin inhibitors and rituximab not curated.

entities.label: Candidate circulating permeability factors
entities.description: Operational serum permeability activity in selected recurrent FSGS; no universal molecular factor identified.

entities.label: Glomerular albumin permeability
entities.description: Albumin permeability in an isolated-glomerulus assay; distinct from clinical proteinuria.

entities.label: Post-transplant FSGS recurrence
entities.description: Recurrent primary FSGS in selected transplant cohorts.

entities.label: Anti-nephrin autoantibodies
entities.description: Nephrin-reactive serum antibodies reported in subsets; assay specificity and disease enrichment remain contested.

entities.label: Nephrin
entities.description: Slit-diaphragm protein tested as an autoantigen; no NPHS1 monogenic disease branch.

entities.label: Primary FSGS phenotype
entities.description: Biopsy-defined primary FSGS in cited human cohorts, distinguished from APOL1-associated disease.

entities.label: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor
entities.description: Candidate circulating factor studied in podocyte assays; serum measurements lack consistent diagnostic specificity.

entities.label: Anti-CD40 autoantibodies
entities.description: Patient-derived antibodies tested in cultured human podocyte injury assays.

entities.label: Podocytes
entities.description: Glomerular epithelial cells studied in human cultures and experimental animal models; individual evidence specifies the system.

entities.label: Podocyte depletion
entities.description: Experimentally induced podocyte loss in toxin-receptor transgenic rats; model of a final injury pathway.

entities.label: Segmental glomerulosclerosis
entities.description: Segmental glomerular scarring; a histologic injury pattern with heterogeneous causes.

entities.label: Proteinuria
entities.description: Urinary protein excretion; a surrogate distinct from kidney-function preservation.

entities.label: Interferon gamma
entities.description: Type II interferon used to induce endogenous APOL1-associated currents in primary human podocytes.

entities.label: APOL1 risk-variant protein
entities.description: APOL1 G1/G2 branch; a genetic susceptibility route separate from idiopathic primary FSGS.

entities.label: APOL1-mediated cation transport
entities.description: APOL1-associated monovalent ion flux measured in cultured cells and transgenic models.

entities.label: Inaxaplin
entities.description: Small-molecule APOL1 channel inhibitor examined in preclinical experiments and a phase 2a uncontrolled trial.

entities.label: Sparsentan
entities.description: Dual endothelin/angiotensin receptor antagonist evaluated in DUPLEX; current US indication is phenotype restricted.

claims.text: Serum from recurrent FSGS patients increased albumin permeability in an isolated-glomerulus assay.
limitations: Ex vivo assay does not identify the factor, prove clinical causation, or apply to all primary FSGS.

claims.text: Circulating permeability activity was associated with FSGS recurrence after transplantation.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: Anti-nephrin antibodies were detected in 7 of 74 adults (9%) with primary FSGS in the multicenter study.
limitations: Minority subgroup; activity correlations and experimental MCD-like findings cannot be assigned to all FSGS.

claims.text: Nephrin-directed antibodies localized to the slit diaphragm in an active-immunization mouse model.
limitations: MCD-like mouse model; not a demonstration of human FSGS sclerosis or universal antibody causation.

claims.text: A Chinese cohort including 160 primary FSGS and 436 MCD patients reported anti-nephrin reactivity; its 43% overall prevalence is pooled across diagnoses.
limitations: Pooled result must not be reported as FSGS-specific prevalence; assay/cohort differences remain unresolved.

claims.text: A separate podocytopathy cohort found very low anti-nephrin prevalence with human-cell antigen and no disease enrichment, challenging broad biomarker interpretation.
limitations: Mixed podocytopathies, not a primary-FSGS-only estimate; does not exclude a rare pathogenic subset.
Antigen-dependent cross-reactivity materially limits cross-study comparison.

claims.text: suPAR-associated podocyte injury in patient-serum culture assays was inhibited by anti-uPAR blockade.
limitations: Culture blockade does not establish suPAR as a universal circulating cause or an effective clinical target.

claims.text: Patient-derived anti-CD40 antibodies were studied in human podocyte injury assays with rescue by pathway blockade.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: Serum suPAR was not significantly higher in the FSGS group in a prospective Brazilian biopsy cohort.
limitations: FSGS classification not restricted to primary disease; biomarker specificity test does not directly refute culture toxicity.
Indirect qualification of generalizing the suPAR injury hypothesis; this is a biomarker null finding, not a direct culture replication.

claims.text: Interferon gamma induced an APOL1-dependent cation current in primary human podocytes.
limitations: Culture response; not proof that interferon is required in every APOL1-associated patient.

claims.text: Induced G1 expression produced sodium import and potassium efflux in HEK293 experiments.
limitations: Overexpression system; G1 result does not by itself establish identical G2 effects or penetrance in humans.

claims.text: IFNγ-induced APOL1 G1 in transgenic mouse podocytes produced ion-flux and injury phenotypes reversible by VX-147.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: Inaxaplin inhibited APOL1 channel function in preclinical cell assays.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: In a single-group phase 2a study, 13 adherent participants with two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS had a mean 47.6% proteinuria reduction at 13 weeks.
limitations: Uncontrolled small short-term trial; no randomized effect estimate, established kidney-survival benefit or approval inference.

claims.text: Toxin-induced podocyte depletion produced focal segmental sclerosis in transgenic rats.
limitations: Generic final-pathway animal model; does not establish the initiating mechanism in primary human FSGS.

claims.text: Increasing experimental podocyte depletion caused persistent proteinuria in transgenic rats.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: DUPLEX showed greater partial proteinuria remission with sparsentan than irbesartan at 36 weeks (42% versus 26%).
limitations: Mixed FSGS eligibility; not proof of immunologic mechanism or applicability of current indication to nephrotic primary FSGS.

claims.text: Despite greater proteinuria reduction, DUPLEX found no significant between-group eGFR-slope difference at 108 weeks.
limitations: Surrogate improvement must not be described as demonstrated overall trial kidney-function preservation.

claims.text: Inaxaplin inhibited APOL1 channel function in preclinical cell assays.
limitations: Abstract-level inspection; no independent domain review or complete methods appraisal.

claims.text: In a single-group phase 2a study, 13 adherent participants with two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS had a mean 47.6% proteinuria reduction at 13 weeks.
limitations: Uncontrolled small short-term trial; no randomized effect estimate, established kidney-survival benefit or approval inference.

claims.text: DUPLEX showed greater partial proteinuria remission with sparsentan than irbesartan at 36 weeks (42% versus 26%).
limitations: Mixed FSGS eligibility; not proof of immunologic mechanism or applicability of current indication to nephrotic primary FSGS.

claims.text: Despite greater proteinuria reduction, DUPLEX found no significant between-group eGFR-slope difference at 108 weeks.
limitations: Surrogate improvement must not be described as demonstrated overall trial kidney-function preservation.

claims.text: In the United States, sparsentan is approved to reduce proteinuria in patients aged eight years and older with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome.
limitations: Label restriction excludes nephrotic syndrome; no extrapolation to nephrotic primary FSGS.

therapies.name: Inaxaplin (VX-147)
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits APOL1 channel function in preclinical assays.
therapies.indication: Investigational APOL1-associated proteinuric kidney disease; initial trial required two APOL1 risk variants and biopsy-proven FSGS.
therapies.trialPhase: Inspected efficacy report: phase 2a (NCT04340362); subsequent development not systematically curated
limitations: Small uncontrolled 13-week study; no randomized kidney-outcome efficacy established.
2026 sponsor updates identified in search; newer trial results not independently inspected or mapped.

therapies.name: Sparsentan (Filspari)
therapies.modality: Oral dual endothelin / angiotensin II receptor antagonist
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Dual endothelin and angiotensin II receptor antagonism, as described by FDA; specific receptor nodes not expanded in this map.
therapies.indication: US: reduce proteinuria in patients aged eight years and older with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome.
limitations: US label excludes nephrotic syndrome; not an approved treatment for the nephrotic primary-FSGS branch.
DUPLEX overall eGFR-slope endpoint was not significant despite proteinuria improvement.
FDA announcement notes hepatotoxicity/REMS; full prescribing information not appraised.
